persona.title: Pretend you are…
persona.text: Pretend you are Njeri, 21, visiting your grandmother, Cucu Wambui, 74, in Murang'a. She takes blood pressure pills, walks to her shamba, goes to market and to church, and she often forgets the pills. Her son Kamau in Nairobi worries about her. Today you are setting up Every Day on Cucu's phone for her.

lines: Welcome. This short video explains an app called Every Day. In about three minutes you will know what it is for and how to use it.

First, the problem. The small things in a day slip away. A short walk. Taking your pills. Calling someone. Drinking water. Not because we do not care, but because nothing reminds us, and nothing notices when we do them.

Every Day is for anyone, but it was made especially for older people. Think of a grandmother who must take her pills every morning and evening, and whose children live far away and want to know she is fine.
Here is the whole idea. Each small thing is a card, like a playing card. When you have done it today, you tap the card. That is all.

lines.t: At the top is the helper line. It tells you, in plain words, what is still left to do today.
Under it are three numbers. Today shows how many of today's cards are done. Best run is the most days in a row you kept one card going. Perfect this week counts the days when every card was done.
Then the week, Monday to Sunday. A gold day means everything was done that day.

Then the cards. Each card has a picture, a name, and a big number. The big number is the run: how many days in a row it has been done. Tap a card when it is done, and it turns gold with a tick. Tap again to undo a mistake.

lines: If a card says not today, it is not due today, so it cannot break the run.
To make a new card, tap the card with the plus sign, called Add a card. Type a few words, like Walk to the shamba. Tap a picture.
Then choose How often. On set days means every day, or only the days you tap, like only Sunday. Some times a week means, for example, three times a week on any days you like.

Pills are special. Under More than once a day, you can add a line for each time, like Morning and Evening. Then one card gets a separate tick for each time, and the card is done when all the ticks are done.
Tap Save. To change or remove a card later, tap Change or remove a card. Every card also keeps a History, showing each day it was done.

lines.t: Now the button called Settings, I am OK text, day off. Inside is Let someone know I am OK. You type the name and mobile number of one or two people, like a son in Nairobi.

lines: When the last card of the day is done, the app gets a short text message ready that says I am OK, and what was done today. The phone does not send it by itself. You tap, your messages open, and you press Send yourself.
In the same Settings there is Sick day. If you are unwell, take the day off, and your runs stay safe. You can do this once every seven days.
Everything stays on this phone. There is no account, and the app is free.
To start again with no cards, use Take the tour again under the question mark button, then Start fresh. Then remove any cards that are left. The test tells you exactly how.

In the test, you will be Njeri, setting up the app for your grandmother. Take your time, read the words on the screen, and if something is confusing, say so. Confusing parts are exactly what we want to find.

challenge.intro: Now you are Njeri, setting up Cucu Wambui's phone in Murang'a. The app must start empty. Nobody will tell you which button to press: use what you learned. You do NOT need to send any real text message. When you finish, tap Check my work.
challenge.start: Use the NORMAL app link (not the 🧪 test copy). Open Every Day. This app is not in the house erase list, so there is no 🧹 Start fresh link at the bottom. Instead: 1) If the welcome tour shows by itself, tap 'skip the tour' → '✨ Start fresh with my own' → OK. If it does not show, tap the ? button at the bottom right → '🎬 Take the tour again' → 'skip the tour' → '✨ Start fresh with my own' → OK. This removes the six example cards. 2) If any cards are still there, tap '✏️ Change or remove a card' → tap the card's name → '🗑 Remove' → OK. Repeat until no cards are left. 3) Tap '⚙️ Settings · I’m OK text · day off' → 'Let someone know I’m OK'. If it says On, open it and tap 'Turn off'. Close Settings. The screen now says 'Make a card'. (Verified 10 Oct: all six checks false after this.)

tasks.text: Cucu walks to her shamba every day. Make a card for it.
tasks.hint: Use the card with the plus sign. Put the word shamba in its name, and choose every day.

tasks.text: Cucu takes blood pressure pills twice a day: in the morning and in the evening. Make ONE card for her pills that gets a separate tick for each time.
tasks.check: (function(){try{var d=JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('dj_everyday_v1')||'null');if(!d||!Array.isArray(d.habits))return false;return d.habits.some(function(h){var ds=Array.isArray(h.doses)?h.doses:[];if(ds.length<2)return false;var l=ds.map(function(x){return String(x.label||'').toLowerCase()});return l.some(function(s){return s.indexOf('morn')>=0})&&l.some(function(s){return s.indexOf('even')>=0})})}catch(e){return false}})()
tasks.hint: Two separate cards is not right. Open one card and look for 'More than once a day? (pills)'.

tasks.text: Cucu goes to church on Sundays only. Make a card for church that is due only on Sunday.
tasks.hint: Under 'How often?', choose 'On set days', and leave only Sun chosen.

tasks.text: Cucu goes to the market about three times a week, on any days she likes. Make a card for the market that fits.
tasks.hint: It is not every day. Look under 'How often?' for 'Some times a week'.

tasks.text: Her son Kamau (mobile 0712 345 678) wants to know she is OK each day. Set the app so it offers to tell Kamau she is OK. Do not send a real message.
tasks.hint: Look in '⚙️ Settings' for 'Let someone know I’m OK'. Type Kamau's name AND number, then Save.

tasks.text: Today Cucu already walked to her shamba. Show that it is done today.
tasks.check: (function(){try{var d=JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('dj_everyday_v1')||'null');if(!d||!Array.isArray(d.habits))return false;var t=new Date();var k=t.getFullYear()+'-'+String(t.getMonth()+1).padStart(2,'0')+'-'+String(t.getDate()).padStart(2,'0');var lg=(d.log||{})[k]||{};return d.habits.some(function(h){return /shamba/i.test(String(h.name||''))&&!!lg[h.id]})}catch(e){return false}})()
tasks.hint: Tap the shamba card itself. It turns gold with a tick.

ownWords.question: In your own words, what is this app for?
keyIdeas: remembering small daily things (walk, pills, a call) by tapping a card when it is done
it counts how many days in a row you keep each one going
it can get an I am OK text ready for family far away

daily.task: Tick today’s cards in Every Day as you do them — or add one new card for something you do every day.
